indicator.name: CoinMarketCap Crypto Market Metrics
indicator.description: A market-wide daily snapshot from CoinMarketCap containing aggregate cryptocurrency market capitalization, trading volume, market-share measures, sector-level market capitalization and volume, derivatives activity, market growth rates, and ecosystem activity statistics. The dataset provides a broad view of crypto-market size, liquidity, market structure, capital distribution, and changes in market activity within a single observation.
indicator.use: Monitor the overall size, liquidity, composition, activity, and structural changes of the cryptocurrency market using CoinMarketCap's aggregate market metrics.
indicator.purpose: Provide a consolidated market-wide snapshot for understanding total crypto-market capitalization, trading activity, Bitcoin and Ethereum market share, altcoin and DeFi market size, stablecoin liquidity, derivatives activity, and changes in the broader crypto ecosystem.
indicator.significance: CoinMarketCap Crypto Market Metrics provides broad market context that can be used to interpret changes across individual crypto assets and specialized indicators. Total market capitalization measures the aggregate value of the cryptocurrency market, while 24-hour spot trading volume provides a measure of market activity and liquidity. Altcoin market capitalization and volume help isolate activity outside Bitcoin, while Bitcoin and Ethereum dominance measure their respective shares of the total cryptocurrency market and can provide context for capital distribution and rotation. DeFi market capitalization and volume provide visibility into decentralized-finance activity, while stablecoin market capitalization and volume provide context for the size and activity of crypto-native liquidity instruments. Derivatives volume provides a measure of activity in crypto derivatives markets. The dataset also includes daily percentage changes in total market capitalization, total volume, DeFi activity, stablecoin activity, and derivatives activity, allowing the system to identify rapid changes in market conditions. Active cryptocurrency, market-pair, and exchange counts provide additional context for the size and breadth of the crypto ecosystem. These metrics can be analyzed alongside asset prices, market breadth, volatility, derivatives positioning, funding rates, stablecoin indicators, Bitcoin dominance, DeFi indicators, and macroeconomic conditions to identify changes in liquidity, market participation, capital rotation, and broader crypto-market regimes.

indicator.name: Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index
indicator.description: A daily composite index from Alternative.me measuring crypto-market sentiment on a scale from 0 to 100, where lower values represent greater fear and higher values represent greater greed. Alternative.me derives the index from multiple sentiment-related inputs, including Bitcoin volatility, market momentum and volume, social media activity, surveys, Bitcoin dominance, and Google Trends. Alternative.me's published methodology currently identifies the index as Bitcoin-focused.
indicator.use: Track daily changes in aggregate crypto-market sentiment using Alternative.me's composite Fear & Greed Index and its fear-to-greed classification.
indicator.purpose: Provide a standardized daily measure of market sentiment that can be used to identify shifts between fear, neutrality, and greed in the crypto market.
indicator.significance: The Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index combines multiple market and sentiment signals into a single 0-to-100 measure. Alternative.me's published methodology assigns 25% weight to volatility, 25% to market momentum and volume, 15% to social media, 15% to surveys, 10% to Bitcoin dominance, and 10% to Google Trends, although Alternative.me currently states that its surveys are paused. The index therefore captures several dimensions of market behavior rather than directly measuring investor sentiment through a single survey. It can be analyzed alongside price trends, volatility, trading volume, derivatives positioning, funding rates, market breadth, Bitcoin dominance, and other sentiment indicators to provide broader context for changes in crypto-market conditions.

indicator.name: CoinMarketCap Altcoin Season Index
indicator.description: A daily CoinMarketCap index measuring the relative performance of major altcoins versus Bitcoin over a rolling 90-day period. The index uses the top 100 eligible coins ranked on CoinMarketCap, excluding stablecoins and wrapped or asset-backed tokens, and scales the proportion of coins outperforming Bitcoin to a 0-to-100 index.
indicator.use: Track the degree to which major altcoins are outperforming or underperforming Bitcoin over a rolling 90-day period and identify shifts between Bitcoin-dominant and altcoin-dominant market regimes.
indicator.purpose: Provide a standardized measure of altcoin market breadth relative to Bitcoin and identify broad changes in relative performance across the cryptocurrency market.
indicator.significance: The CoinMarketCap Altcoin Season Index measures market breadth by comparing the rolling 90-day performance of the top 100 eligible coins on CoinMarketCap against Bitcoin. Stablecoins and wrapped or asset-backed tokens are excluded from the constituent set. The index reflects the proportion of these coins outperforming Bitcoin and is scaled from 1 to 100. Values above 75 indicate Altcoin Season, while values at or below 25 indicate Bitcoin Season. The index therefore measures the breadth of altcoin outperformance rather than sentiment directly: a high value means a large share of major altcoins have outperformed Bitcoin over the measurement period, while a low value means relatively few have done so. It can be analyzed alongside Bitcoin dominance, altcoin market capitalization, market breadth, liquidity, trading volume, and crypto-market sentiment to provide context for changes in market regime and capital rotation.

indicator.name: XRP Spot ETF Market
indicator.description: A daily measure of U.S. spot XRP ETF market activity, including aggregate net capital flows, traded value, net assets, and cumulative net flows. The indicator provides a view of capital entering or leaving XRP spot ETF vehicles and the size and activity of regulated investment products providing traditional investors with access to XRP.
indicator.use: Track daily capital flows, trading activity, assets under management, and cumulative capital flows in the U.S. spot XRP ETF market.
indicator.purpose: Provide a daily view of traditional-finance and institutional market participation in XRP through regulated spot ETF vehicles and identify changes in capital allocation toward XRP.
indicator.significance: XRP spot ETF market data provides a view of capital flows and asset levels within regulated investment vehicles that give traditional investors access to XRP. Net flow measures the daily net movement of capital into or out of the ETF market, while value traded measures ETF trading activity. Net assets indicate the aggregate size of assets held through the ETF vehicles, and cumulative net flow tracks the longer-term accumulation of capital flows. XRP ETF activity can provide context for traditional-finance participation in XRP and can be analyzed alongside XRP price, XRP Ledger activity, transaction activity, payment and settlement use cases, cross-border payment infrastructure, derivatives positioning, macroeconomic conditions, liquidity conditions, and broader crypto-market sentiment. ETF flows should be interpreted as activity within the spot XRP ETF market and should not be treated as a complete measure of all institutional XRP ownership or total XRP demand.

indicator.name: CFTC Bitcoin Futures Positioning
indicator.description: A weekly measure of Bitcoin futures open interest and trader positioning reported by the CFTC's Traders in Financial Futures report. The data separates Bitcoin futures positions into Dealer/Intermediary, Asset Manager/Institutional, Leveraged Money, Other Reportables, and Nonreportables, with long, short, spreading, and net exposure measures where applicable.
indicator.use: Track changes in Bitcoin futures open interest and positioning across dealers, asset managers, leveraged funds, other reportable traders, and nonreportable traders, including shifts in long, short, spreading, and net exposure.
indicator.purpose: Provide asset-specific visibility into how different classes of market participants are positioned in Bitcoin futures and how their exposure changes over time.
indicator.significance: CFTC Bitcoin futures positioning provides a structured view of institutional, leveraged, dealer, and other trader exposure to Bitcoin through regulated futures markets. Changes in open interest reveal changes in futures-market participation, while changes in long and short positions show how each trader group is adjusting directional exposure. Separating trader classifications allows the intelligence system to distinguish institutional and leveraged positioning from dealer activity and aggregate nonreportable participation when analyzing Bitcoin market structure and sentiment.

indicator.name: CFTC Ethereum Futures Positioning
indicator.description: A weekly measure of Ethereum futures open interest and trader positioning reported by the CFTC's Traders in Financial Futures report. The data separates Ethereum futures positions into Dealer/Intermediary, Asset Manager/Institutional, Leveraged Funds, Other Reportables, and Nonreportables, with long, short, spreading, and net exposure measures where applicable. Each Ethereum futures contract represents 50 ETH.
indicator.use: Track changes in Ethereum futures open interest and positioning across dealers, asset managers, leveraged funds, other reportable traders, and nonreportable traders, including changes in long, short, spreading, and net exposure.
indicator.purpose: Provide asset-specific visibility into how different classes of market participants are positioned in Ethereum futures and how their exposure changes over time.
indicator.significance: CFTC Ethereum futures positioning provides a structured view of institutional, leveraged, dealer, and other trader exposure to Ethereum through regulated futures markets. Changes in open interest reveal changes in futures-market participation, while changes in long and short positions show how each trader group is adjusting exposure to Ethereum. Because Ethereum is a major cryptoasset with substantial derivatives activity, futures positioning can provide context for Ethereum market structure, institutional participation, derivatives-market sentiment, risk appetite, and changes in exposure to the broader crypto market.

indicator.name: CFTC Micro Ether Futures Positioning
indicator.description: A weekly measure of Micro Ether futures open interest and trader positioning reported by the CFTC's Traders in Financial Futures report. The data separates Micro Ether futures positions into Dealer/Intermediary, Asset Manager/Institutional, Leveraged Funds, Other Reportables, and Nonreportables, with long, short, spreading, and net exposure measures where applicable. Each Micro Ether futures contract represents 0.1 ETH.
indicator.use: Track changes in Micro Ether futures open interest and positioning across dealers, asset managers, leveraged funds, other reportable traders, and nonreportable traders, including changes in long, short, spreading, and net exposure.
indicator.purpose: Provide asset-specific visibility into how different classes of market participants are positioned in Micro Ether futures and how their exposure changes over time.
indicator.significance: CFTC Micro Ether futures positioning provides a structured view of trader exposure to Ethereum through a smaller-sized regulated futures contract. Changes in open interest reveal changes in participation in the Micro Ether futures market, while changes in long and short positions show how different trader groups are adjusting their Ethereum exposure. Because each contract represents 0.1 ETH, the Micro Ether contract provides a lower-contract-size representation of Ethereum derivatives positioning that complements standard Ether futures data and can provide additional context for crypto market structure, trader positioning, institutional and leveraged activity, and Ethereum derivatives-market conditions.

indicator.name: CNN Fear & Greed Index
indicator.description: A daily composite index designed by CNN to measure prevailing fear and greed in the U.S. stock market using multiple market-behavior indicators. The index ranges from 0 to 100, with lower values representing greater fear and higher values representing greater greed.
indicator.use: Monitor changes in U.S. equity-market sentiment, investor risk appetite, market momentum, volatility, and demand for defensive assets, and identify shifts between risk-seeking and risk-averse market conditions.
indicator.purpose: Provide a compact market-sentiment signal that summarizes several observable characteristics of U.S. equity markets into a single daily measure for tracking changes in investor risk appetite and market stress.
indicator.significance: The Fear & Greed Index provides a behavioral measure of the prevailing emotional conditions in U.S. equity markets. Changes in the index can indicate shifts in market momentum, volatility, demand for safe-haven assets, and willingness to take risk. It can therefore provide context for interpreting market moves alongside prices, volatility measures, credit conditions, and broader financial-market indicators.

indicator.name: CNN Market Volatility (VIX vs 50-Day Moving Average)
indicator.description: A daily market-volatility indicator based on the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) relative to its 50-day moving average. The VIX reflects expected S&P 500 volatility over the following 30 days, while its relationship with the 50-day average is used by CNN as a measure of changing market volatility and fear.
indicator.use: Monitor changes in expected U.S. equity-market volatility and identify shifts in market stress, risk aversion, and investor sentiment through the VIX's relationship with its 50-day trend.
indicator.purpose: Provide a volatility-based measure of U.S. equity-market conditions that captures whether expected market volatility is increasing or decreasing relative to its recent trend.
indicator.significance: The VIX provides a forward-looking measure of expected S&P 500 volatility derived from options prices. Comparing it with its 50-day moving average adds a trend dimension that helps identify changes in market stress and risk perception. Rising volatility relative to its trend is interpreted by CNN as a signal of fear, while declining volatility is associated with greed. As one component of the Fear & Greed framework, it complements momentum, breadth, options positioning, and other measures of market behavior.

indicator.name: CNN Safe Haven Demand
indicator.description: A daily measure of the difference between U.S. Treasury bond and stock returns over the previous 20 trading days. It is used by CNN to assess whether investors are favoring safer Treasury assets over riskier equities.
indicator.use: Monitor shifts between equity risk-taking and demand for safer Treasury assets, and identify changes in investor risk appetite, defensive positioning, and market stress.
indicator.purpose: Provide a cross-asset measure of investor risk preference by comparing recent stock and Treasury performance over a 20-trading-day period.
indicator.significance: Safe Haven Demand captures changes in investor preference between riskier equities and safer Treasury assets. When Treasury bonds outperform stocks, it can indicate increased demand for defensive assets and greater risk aversion; when stocks outperform Treasuries, it indicates stronger relative demand for risk assets. As a component of CNN's Fear & Greed framework, it adds a cross-asset risk-preference signal that complements equity momentum, breadth, volatility, and options positioning.

indicator.name: AAII Investor Sentiment Survey
indicator.description: A weekly survey of individual investors measuring the percentage who expect the U.S. stock market to rise, remain essentially unchanged, or fall over the next six months. The dataset includes bullish, neutral, bearish, and bull-bear spread readings.
indicator.use: Monitor changes in individual-investor expectations, optimism, pessimism, uncertainty, and overall sentiment toward the U.S. stock market, including changes in the bull-bear spread.
indicator.purpose: Provide a direct survey-based measure of individual-investor expectations that complements market-derived sentiment indicators by capturing what retail investors expect the stock market to do over the following six months.
indicator.significance: The AAII Sentiment Survey provides a direct measure of individual-investor expectations rather than inferring sentiment from market prices or positioning. Changes in bullish, neutral, and bearish responses reveal shifts in optimism, pessimism, and uncertainty, while the bull-bear spread summarizes the balance between optimistic and pessimistic views. Extreme sentiment readings can provide useful context for assessing investor psychology and potential sentiment reversals, but the survey does not establish the future direction of the market.

indicator.name: IG Gold Retail Positioning
indicator.description: A daily measure of long and short positioning among retail traders on the IG trading platform for gold. The indicator reports the percentage of IG retail traders holding long and short positions and the resulting net positioning. This data represents IG's own retail trader pool and is not a market-wide measure of all retail traders or investors.
indicator.use: Track daily changes in long and short positioning among IG retail traders exposed to gold, including the distribution of positions and the resulting net retail positioning.
indicator.purpose: Provide a daily view of how IG's retail trader population is positioned toward gold and how that positioning changes over time.
indicator.significance: IG gold retail positioning provides a daily view of directional exposure among retail traders using the IG trading platform. The indicator can provide context for retail sentiment, speculative positioning, and changes in exposure to gold. Because the dataset represents only IG's retail trader pool rather than the entire retail-investor population, it should be interpreted as a broker-specific positioning signal rather than a comprehensive measure of overall retail sentiment. Gold positioning can be analyzed alongside gold prices, safe-haven demand, inflation expectations, real interest rates, Treasury yields, the U.S. dollar, Federal Reserve policy, and broader financial-market conditions to provide additional context for changes in gold-market positioning.

items.headline: Bitcoin compresses the range and builds pressure for a run
items.summary: Bitcoin is trading in a narrow range so far today, with a low of $85,131 and a high of $86,375. The current price is near $86,163, toward the upper end of that range. The buyers have a modest technical advantage. However, they still need to clear overhead resistance to give the next move higher more momentum. In the video above, I take a detailed look at the digital currency and explain in detail the compression and what traders should be on the lookout for.   Rising moving averages support the buyers The price has dipped briefly below its rising 100-hour moving average at $85,373, but those breaks have been modest and have failed to attract sustained selling. That suggests buyers remain willing to step in on dips. Below that, the 200-hour moving average at $84,633 provides another support target, followed by the rising 100-bar moving average on the 4-hour chart near $84,393. Together, those moving averages give traders a series of levels to measure the buyers’ control. Holding above them keeps the recovery intact. Breaking below them would start to take that control away. The upper swing area remains a hurdle On the topside, Bitcoin remains within the $85,578–$87,374 swing area that has been in play since late September. That area also has a longer history. It acted as a floor from late December into late January before the price broke lower on January 29. An old floor can become a ceiling when the price returns to it from below, as traders use those familiar levels to sell or reduce exposure. The buyers have worked their way back into that area. Now they need to get through the top. A move above $87,374—and the ability to stay above it—would increase the bullish bias and open the door for further upside momentum. Bitcoin is compressing like a spring With rising support underneath and resistance overhead, Bitcoin’s price action resembles a spring being compressed. At some point, that compression releases. When it does, the move can be quick as traders caught on the wrong side adjust their positions and breakout traders join the move. The challenge is that compression does not tell us which direction the price will break. The technical levels help answer that question. For Bitcoin, $87,374 is the key upside trigger, while a break below the support cluster extending down to $84,393 would give sellers more control. Until then, traders are waiting for the next shove. Key technical levels An upside break above $87,374 would have traders targeting: $90,000: Natural round-number resistance. $90,554: Swing high resistance from late January. $92,000: The 50% midpoint of the decline from the October all-time high. On the downside, sellers first need to break the 100-hour moving average at $85,373, followed by the 200-hour moving average at $84,633 and the 4-hour chart’s 100-bar moving average near $84,393. Below that support, the next targets are: $83,916: The previously broken 38.2% retracement. $81,517–$82,833: A lower swing area. $81,404: The rising 200-bar moving average on the 4-hour chart. Trader education: A break needs follow-through For newer traders, the lesson is that a brief move through a technical level is only the first step. The price needs to stay beyond that level and attract follow-through. Today’s modest dips below the 100-hour moving average show why that matters. Sellers had an opportunity, but they could not build momentum. The same test applies at $87,374. Break above and hold, and buyers strengthen their case. Break above and fall back below, and the buyers may have had their shot—and missed. Know the levels before the spring releases. They help you define your risk, limit your risk and judge whether the next shove is gaining traction. This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

items.headline: Bitcoin compresses the range and builds pressure for a run
items.summary: Bitcoin is trading in a narrow range so far today, with a low of $85,131 and a high of $86,375. The current price is near $86,163, toward the upper end of that range. The buyers have a modest technical advantage. However, they still need to clear overhead resistance to give the next move higher more momentum. In the video above, I take a detailed look at the digital currency and explain in detail the compression and what traders should be on the lookout for.   Rising moving averages support the buyers The price has dipped briefly below its rising 100-hour moving average at $85,373, but those breaks have been modest and have failed to attract sustained selling. That suggests buyers remain willing to step in on dips. Below that, the 200-hour moving average at $84,633 provides another support target, followed by the rising 100-bar moving average on the 4-hour chart near $84,393. Together, those moving averages give traders a series of levels to measure the buyers’ control. Holding above them keeps the recovery intact. Breaking below them would start to take that control away. The upper swing area remains a hurdle On the topside, Bitcoin remains within the $85,578–$87,374 swing area that has been in play since late September. That area also has a longer history. It acted as a floor from late December into late January before the price broke lower on January 29. An old floor can become a ceiling when the price returns to it from below, as traders use those familiar levels to sell or reduce exposure. The buyers have worked their way back into that area. Now they need to get through the top. A move above $87,374—and the ability to stay above it—would increase the bullish bias and open the door for further upside momentum. Bitcoin is compressing like a spring With rising support underneath and resistance overhead, Bitcoin’s price action resembles a spring being compressed. At some point, that compression releases. When it does, the move can be quick as traders caught on the wrong side adjust their positions and breakout traders join the move. The challenge is that compression does not tell us which direction the price will break. The technical levels help answer that question. For Bitcoin, $87,374 is the key upside trigger, while a break below the support cluster extending down to $84,393 would give sellers more control. Until then, traders are waiting for the next shove. Key technical levels An upside break above $87,374 would have traders targeting: $90,000: Natural round-number resistance. $90,554: Swing high resistance from late January. $92,000: The 50% midpoint of the decline from the October all-time high. On the downside, sellers first need to break the 100-hour moving average at $85,373, followed by the 200-hour moving average at $84,633 and the 4-hour chart’s 100-bar moving average near $84,393. Below that support, the next targets are: $83,916: The previously broken 38.2% retracement. $81,517–$82,833: A lower swing area. $81,404: The rising 200-bar moving average on the 4-hour chart. Trader education: A break needs follow-through For newer traders, the lesson is that a brief move through a technical level is only the first step. The price needs to stay beyond that level and attract follow-through. Today’s modest dips below the 100-hour moving average show why that matters. Sellers had an opportunity, but they could not build momentum. The same test applies at $87,374. Break above and hold, and buyers strengthen their case. Break above and fall back below, and the buyers may have had their shot—and missed. Know the levels before the spring releases. They help you define your risk, limit your risk and judge whether the next shove is gaining traction. This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

"summary": "Bitcoin is trading in a narrow range so far today, with a low of $85,131 and a high of $86,375. The current price is near $86,163, toward the upper end of that range. The buyers have a modest technical advantage. However, they still need to clear overhead resistance to give the next move higher more momentum. In the video above, I take a detailed look at the digital currency and explain in detail the compression and what traders should be on the lookout for.   Rising moving averages support the buyers The price has dipped briefly below its rising 100-hour moving average at $85,373, but those breaks have been modest and have failed to attract sustained selling. That suggests buyers remain willing to step in on dips. Below that, the 200-hour moving average at $84,633 provides another support target, followed by the rising 100-bar moving average on the 4-hour chart near $84,393. Together, those moving averages give traders a series of levels to measure the buyers’ control. Holding above them keeps the recovery intact. Breaking below them would start to take that control away. The upper swing area remains a hurdle On the topside, Bitcoin remains within the $85,578–$87,374 swing area that has been in play since late September. That area also has a longer history. It acted as a floor from late December into late January before the price broke lower on January 29. An old floor can become a ceiling when the price returns to it from below, as traders use those familiar levels to sell or reduce exposure. The buyers have worked their way back into that area. Now they need to get through the top. A move above $87,374—and the ability to stay above it—would increase the bullish bias and open the door for further upside momentum. Bitcoin is compressing like a spring With rising support underneath and resistance overhead, Bitcoin’s price action resembles a spring being compressed. At some point, that compression releases. When it does, the move can be quick as traders caught on the wrong side adjust their positions and breakout traders join the move. The challenge is that compression does not tell us which direction the price will break. The technical levels help answer that question. For Bitcoin, $87,374 is the key upside trigger, while a break below the support cluster extending down to $84,393 would give sellers more control. Until then, traders are waiting for the next shove. Key technical levels An upside break above $87,374 would have traders targeting: $90,000: Natural round-number resistance. $90,554: Swing high resistance from late January. $92,000: The 50% midpoint of the decline from the October all-time high. On the downside, sellers first need to break the 100-hour moving average at $85,373, followed by the 200-hour moving average at $84,633 and the 4-hour chart’s 100-bar moving average near $84,393. Below that support, the next targets are: $83,916: The previously broken 38.2% retracement. $81,517–$82,833: A lower swing area. $81,404: The rising 200-bar moving average on the 4-hour chart. Trader education: A break needs follow-through For newer traders, the lesson is that a brief move through a technical level is only the first step. The price needs to stay beyond that level and attract follow-through. Today’s modest dips below the 100-hour moving average show why that matters. Sellers had an opportunity, but they could not build momentum. The same test applies at $87,374. Break above and hold, and buyers strengthen their case. Break above and fall back below, and the buyers may have had their shot—and missed. Know the levels before the spring releases. They help you define your risk, limit your risk and judge whether the next shove is gaining traction. This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com."

"headline": "Bitcoin compresses the range and builds pressure for a run",

"summary": "Bitcoin is trading in a narrow range so far today, with a low of $85,131 and a high of $86,375. The current price is near $86,163, toward the upper end of that range. The buyers have a modest technical advantage. However, they still need to clear overhead resistance to give the next move higher more momentum. In the video above, I take a detailed look at the digital currency and explain in detail the compression and what traders should be on the lookout for.   Rising moving averages support the buyers The price has dipped briefly below its rising 100-hour moving average at $85,373, but those breaks have been modest and have failed to attract sustained selling. That suggests buyers remain willing to step in on dips. Below that, the 200-hour moving average at $84,633 provides another support target, followed by the rising 100-bar moving average on the 4-hour chart near $84,393. Together, those moving averages give traders a series of levels to measure the buyers’ control. Holding above them keeps the recovery intact. Breaking below them would start to take that control away. The upper swing area remains a hurdle On the topside, Bitcoin remains within the $85,578–$87,374 swing area that has been in play since late September. That area also has a longer history. It acted as a floor from late December into late January before the price broke lower on January 29. An old floor can become a ceiling when the price returns to it from below, as traders use those familiar levels to sell or reduce exposure. The buyers have worked their way back into that area. Now they need to get through the top. A move above $87,374—and the ability to stay above it—would increase the bullish bias and open the door for further upside momentum. Bitcoin is compressing like a spring With rising support underneath and resistance overhead, Bitcoin’s price action resembles a spring being compressed. At some point, that compression releases. When it does, the move can be quick as traders caught on the wrong side adjust their positions and breakout traders join the move. The challenge is that compression does not tell us which direction the price will break. The technical levels help answer that question. For Bitcoin, $87,374 is the key upside trigger, while a break below the support cluster extending down to $84,393 would give sellers more control. Until then, traders are waiting for the next shove. Key technical levels An upside break above $87,374 would have traders targeting: $90,000: Natural round-number resistance. $90,554: Swing high resistance from late January. $92,000: The 50% midpoint of the decline from the October all-time high. On the downside, sellers first need to break the 100-hour moving average at $85,373, followed by the 200-hour moving average at $84,633 and the 4-hour chart’s 100-bar moving average near $84,393. Below that support, the next targets are: $83,916: The previously broken 38.2% retracement. $81,517–$82,833: A lower swing area. $81,404: The rising 200-bar moving average on the 4-hour chart. Trader education: A break needs follow-through For newer traders, the lesson is that a brief move through a technical level is only the first step. The price needs to stay beyond that level and attract follow-through. Today’s modest dips below the 100-hour moving average show why that matters. Sellers had an opportunity, but they could not build momentum. The same test applies at $87,374. Break above and hold, and buyers strengthen their case. Break above and fall back below, and the buyers may have had their shot—and missed. Know the levels before the spring releases. They help you define your risk, limit your risk and judge whether the next shove is gaining traction. This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com."
